identity.name: Sucroglycerides
identity.chemical_class: Mixed sucrose-fatty acid ester/glyceride emulsifier system

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic sucrose-derived fatty esters lower interfacial tension and stabilize oil-water dispersions; formulation-dependent effects include texture modification.
common_food_categories: Dairy analogues and frozen dairy desserts

adi.basis: Group ADI for sucrose esters of fatty acids (E473) and sucroglycerides (E474), established by EFSA in 2004 and referenced in EFSA 2018 exposure assessment.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA 2018 exposure assessment (group context E473/E474) reported modeled exceedance of the 40 mg/kg bw/day group ADI in many population groups, especially toddlers and children, with likely overestimation in some scenarios.

adi.basis: Group ADI for sucrose esters of fatty acids and sucroglycerides (latest JECFA evaluation entry).

concerns.summary: Regulatory exposure modeling for the E473/E474 group has reported ADI exceedance in high consumers, particularly children and toddlers.
Human tolerance data reviewed by JECFA left uncertainty about upper-dose gastrointestinal/laxative effects, contributing to a conservative group ADI setting.

no_concern_confirmed: Long-term rat studies on related sucrose ester preparations did not show treatment-related carcinogenicity at tested dietary levels.
No IARC monograph classification entry was identified for sucroglycerides in the current IARC classification dataset reviewed.

adi_exceedance.notes: Exceedance evidence is primarily from group-level EFSA exposure assessments (E473/E474 context), not clearly isolated for E474-only use.

risk_assessment.rationale: E474 is internationally regulated with established group ADIs and without strong carcinogenic classification signals, but repeated group-level ADI exceedance scenarios in children/toddlers and residual GI-tolerance uncertainty at higher intakes support a moderate tier rather than limited.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI context (40 mg/kg bw/day for E473/E474) with exceedance scenarios in young populations
JECFA group ADI 0-30 mg/kg bw and historical GI-tolerance caution
No IARC classification found for sucroglycerides
No major bans identified in reviewed sources
